correctness.rationale: For every odd integer P (negative included), M=[[P,1],[1,0]], det M=-1, and Vn=tr M^n. M^3=PI+(P²+1)M, M^6≡5I mod8. Mod2 the order-three companion implies Vn odd iff 3∤n; V3≡4 mod8 for n≡3 mod6 and duplication V2m=Vm²−2(−1)^m gives valuation 1 for 6|n. The scalar lift M^(3·2^(k−1))≡(1+2^k)I mod2^(k+1) for all k>=2 follows by squaring, and shifts every represented odd residue into its complementary next bit. Initial V1,V2 (P≡1 mod4) or V1,V5 (P≡3 mod4) represent both mod4 odd classes. Hence odd positive-index terms are dense in Z2×, with fixed V1,V6,V3 of valuations 0,1,2; ratios cover the five valuation shells j=-2..2 densely and no others or zero. I independently checked seven positive/negative odd P, full odd-residue coverage modulo 2^k through k=9 and scalar lift through k=8. These finite checks support, but do not replace, the scalar induction.
